title: Python for Data Analysis: Zero to Practical Insights
summary: An 8-week foundational roadmap designed for beginners to confidently clean, transform, analyze, and visualize real-world datasets with Python, NumPy, Pandas, and Seaborn.
assumptions: Workload structured for 5 hours per week with immediate interactive notebook exercises.
Focuses on practical tabular data operations, missing value handling, and exploratory data analysis (EDA).

phases.title: Phase 1: Python Fundamentals & Data Structures
phases.goal: Master Python syntax, collections (lists, dictionaries, sets), and vectorized numerical computation with NumPy.

project.title: Phase 1 Milestone: Multi-Source Sales Transaction Analyzer
project.brief: Write a Python script that ingests multiple messy CSV files, parses date strings, cleans invalid currencies, and computes statistical summaries using NumPy arrays.
acceptance_criteria: Handles corrupted rows without throwing uncaught exceptions
Computes mean, median, standard deviation, and percentiles for revenue
Outputs a formatted summary report to stdout and clean CSV
project.stretch: Benchmark performance difference between Python loops and vectorized NumPy operations.

sessions.title: Python Basics, Control Flow & Data Types

checkpoints.question: Which Python data structure is unordered, mutable, and stores key-value pairs?
checkpoints.explanation: Dictionaries store key-value associations and allow constant-time O(1) lookups.

checkpoints.question: What is the primary difference between a list and a tuple in Python?
options: Lists are mutable while tuples are immutable
There is no difference in behavior
checkpoints.explanation: Tuples cannot be altered once instantiated (immutable), making them safe for static records.
